questions.problem: What is the general solution to the equation $\operatorname{sin}⁡x=1?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the principal value:

$$
{x}_{1}=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(1)=\frac{\pi }{2}
$$

The sine function has a period of $2\pi .$ Hence, the general solution for the given equation is

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{2}+2n\pi .
$$

questions.problem:
Assuming that $n$ is an integer, the general solution to the equation $\operatorname{sin}⁡x=-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$ is given by

$$
x={\theta }_{1}+bn,\,x={\theta }_{2}+bn,
$$

where ${\theta }_{1}<{\theta }_{2}.$ Find the values of ${\theta }_{1}$ and ${\theta }_{2}$ in $[0,2\pi ),$ and the value of $b.$

${\theta }_{1}=${{field-1}}$,\,{\theta }_{2}=$
{{field-2}}$,\,b=$
{{field-3}}
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the principal value:

$$
x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})=-\frac{\pi }{4}
$$

Our first solution lies in the $4$th quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{4}.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x<0,$ the second solution must lie in the third quadrant, and it also has ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{4}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13979076/assets/5af1febb2c8dbf1b19ee64addd8f8ccdd5a30f9330d36ab800475fce9f6740c2.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$  lies in the $3$rd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\pi +{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi +\frac{\pi }{4} \\  & =\frac{5\pi }{4}\end{aligned}
$$

The general solution for the given equation is 

$$
x=-\frac{\pi }{4}+2n\pi ,\,x=\frac{5\pi }{4}+2n\pi .
$$

Writing this as $x=\theta +2n\pi ,$ where $\theta \in [0,2\pi ),$ we get

$$
x=\frac{7\pi }{4}+2n\pi ,\,x=\frac{5\pi }{4}+2n\pi .
$$

Therefore, since ${\theta }_{1}<{\theta }_{2},$ we have ${\theta }_{1}=\frac{5\pi }{4},$ ${\theta }_{2}=\frac{7\pi }{4},$ and $b=2\pi .$

x={45}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘},\,x={315}^{∘}+n\cdot {360}^{∘}.

$$

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡x=\frac{1}{-\sqrt{2}}=-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.
$$

$$
{x}_{1}=\text{arcsin}(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})=-\frac{\pi }{4}
$$

Our first solution lies in the $4$th quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{4}.$ Since $\operatorname{sin}⁡x<0,$ the second solution must lie in the third quadrant, and it also has ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{4}.$

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$  lies in the $3$rd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\pi +{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi +\frac{\pi }{4} \\  & =\frac{5\pi }{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution to the given equation is

$$
x=-\frac{\pi }{4}+2n\pi ,\,x=\frac{5\pi }{4}+2n\pi .
$$

Writing this as $x=\theta +2n\pi ,$ where $\theta \in [0,2\pi ),$ we get

$$
x=\frac{5\pi }{4}+2n\pi ,\,x=\frac{7\pi }{4}+2n\pi .

questions.problem:
Assuming that $n$ is an integer, the general solution to the equation $3\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sec}⁡x-6=0$ is given by 

$$
x={\theta }_{1}+bn,\,x={\theta }_{2}+bn,
$$

where ${\theta }_{1}<{\theta }_{2}.$ Find the values of ${\theta }_{1}$ and ${\theta }_{2}$ in $[0,{360}^{∘}),$ and the value of $b.$

${\theta }_{1}=${{field-1}}${}^{∘},\,{\theta }_{2}=$
{{field-2}}${}^{∘},\,b=$
{{field-3}}${}^{∘}$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation and isolate $\operatorname{sec}⁡x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sec}⁡x-6 & =0 \\ 3\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sec}⁡x & =6 \\ \operatorname{sec}⁡x & =\frac{6}{3\sqrt{2}}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}=\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that $\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}.$ Therefore, the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
{x}_{1}=\text{arccos}(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})={45}^{∘}
$$

Our first solution lies in the $1$st quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}={45}^{∘}.$ Since $\operatorname{cos}⁡x>0,$ the second solution must lie in the fourth quadrant, and it also has ${\theta }_{R}={45}^{∘}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13979076/assets/cf16066cb8b8368129be39a22f5c15727ac698f44d6f870511c2e07ec317d643.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$  lies in the $4$th quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={360}^{∘}-{\theta }_{R} \\  & ={360}^{∘}-{45}^{∘} \\  & ={315}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

The general solution for the given equation is

$$
x={45}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}n,\,x={315}^{∘}+{360}^{∘}n.
$$

Therefore, since ${\theta }_{1}<{\theta }_{2},$ we have ${\theta }_{1}=45\,{\,}^{∘},$ ${\theta }_{2}=315\,{\,}^{∘},$ and $b=360\,{\,}^{∘}.$

$$

$$
x=\frac{3\pi }{8}+n\pi .

\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\pi -{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi -\frac{\pi }{6} \\  & =\frac{5\pi }{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the general solution for the given equation is

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{6}+2n\pi ,\,x=\frac{5\pi }{6}+2n\pi .
$$

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13979076/assets/6f3382db4b66df920c22c7050ea5e22c56892094c51d8889872b7bfcb541f684.png)

The graph shows a portion of the curve $y=2\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ and the line $y=-\sqrt{2}.$ Find expressions of the form

$$
x={\theta }_{1}+n\cdot b,\,x={\theta }_{2}+n\cdot b,
$$

where ${\theta }_{1}<{\theta }_{2},$ ${\theta }_{1},{\theta }_{2}\in [0,2\pi ),$ $b$ is the period in radians, and $n$ is an integer, that generate the $x$-values of all of their points of intersection.

${\theta }_{1}=${{field-1}}$,\,{\theta }_{2}=$
{{field-2}}$,\,b=$
{{field-3}}
questions.worked_solution:
At the intersection points, the $y$-values are the same for both graphs. This gives the equation

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{cos}⁡x & =-\sqrt{2} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡x & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we find the principal value:

$$
{x}_{1}=arccos\,(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})=\frac{3\pi }{4}.
$$

Our first solution lies in the $2$nd quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}=\pi -\frac{3\pi }{4}=\frac{\pi }{4}.$ 

Since $\operatorname{cos}⁡x<0,$ the second solution must lie in the $3$rd quadrant, and it also has ${\theta }_{R}=\frac{\pi }{4}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13979076/assets/ff58f07acb93044b6bca56ca30fe5f3b8447603ca9cb6d120559d287c435b987.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$  lies in the $3$rd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\pi +{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi +\frac{\pi }{4} \\  & =\frac{5\pi }{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the general solutions are

$$
x=\frac{3\pi }{4}+2\pi n,\,x=\frac{5\pi }{4}+2\pi n.
$$

Therefore, since ${\theta }_{1}<{\theta }_{2},$ we have ${\theta }_{1}=\frac{3\pi }{4},\text{ }{\theta }_{2}=\frac{5\pi }{4},\text{ }\text{and}\text{ }b=2\pi .$

canonical_examples.problem: Find the general solution to $2\cos{x} + \sqrt{2}= 0,$ where $x$ is measured in degrees.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation and isolate $\cos x \mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\sqrt{2} & =0 \\ 2\operatorname{cos}⁡x & =-\sqrt{2} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡x & =-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal value:

$$
x_1 = \arccos\left( -\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \right)= 135^\circ
$$

Our first solution lies in the $2$nd quadrant and has a reference angle of $\theta_R = 45^\circ.$ Since $\cos x<   0,$ the second solution must lie in the third quadrant, and it also has $\theta_R = 45^\circ.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13979076/assets/5f32529ce4132c594d8a886222ff6f1a356eefa95fa4c7e1fd38b9bd4e3932a9.png)

Since the second solution $x_2$  lies in the $3$rd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={180}^{∘}+{\theta }_{R} \\  & ={180}^{∘}+{45}^{∘} \\  & ={225}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solutions for $x\in[0,360)$ are $x=135^\circ, 225^\circ.$ Therefore, the general solution for the given equation, where $n$ is an integer, is

$$
x = 135^\circ+n\cdot 360^\circ, \quad x=225^\circ+n\cdot 360^\circ.
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution to a Trigonometric Equation Containing Secant or Cosecant
canonical_examples.problem: What is the general solution to the equation $3\csc x+2\sqrt{3}=0?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation and isolate $\csc x \mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{csc}⁡x+2\sqrt{3} & =0 \\ 3\operatorname{csc}⁡x & =-2\sqrt{3} \\ \operatorname{csc}⁡x & =-\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that $\csc{x}=\dfrac{1}{\sin{x}}.$ Therefore, the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\sin{x} =-\dfrac{3}{2\sqrt{3}}=-\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})=\frac{5\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Our first solution lies in the $4$th quadrant and has a reference angle of $\theta_R = \dfrac{\pi}{3}.$ Since $\sin x<   0,$ the second solution must lie in the third quadrant, and it also has $\theta_R = \dfrac{\pi}{3}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13979076/assets/0716b8ab50e525f453ae8bc690d404a150f2da98f0a90b6c8856ae9925e7c515.png)

Since the second solution $x_2$  lies in the $3$rd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\pi +{\theta }_{R} \\  & =\pi +\frac{\pi }{3} \\  & =\frac{4\pi }{3}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solutions for $x\in[0,2\pi)$ are $x=\dfrac{4\pi}{3}, \dfrac{5\pi}{3}.$ Therefore, the general solution for the given equation is

$$
x = \dfrac{4\pi}{3}+2n\pi, \quad x=\dfrac{5\pi}{3}+2n\pi,
$$

where $n$ is any integer.

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding the General Solution to a Trigonometric Equation Containing Tangent or Cotangent
canonical_examples.problem: What is the general solution to the equation $\cot{x}=1?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Recall that $\cot{x}=\dfrac{1}{\tan{x}}.$ Therefore, the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡x & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
x_1 = \arctan \left( 1 \right)= \dfrac{\pi}{4}
$$

The tangent function has a period of $\pi.$  Therefore, the general solution for the given equation is: 

$$
x=\dfrac{\pi}{4}+n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is any integer.

canonical_examples.problem:
The graph shows a portion of the curve $y=\sec{x}$ and the line $y=\sqrt{2}.$ What is the general solution for the $x$-values of all of their points of intersection?

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13979076/assets/cae8d73bdf9a21e956c444db4b22bfc26e20b7a9d1593d7759fc119aa4c6a623.png)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
At the intersection points, the $y$-values are the same for both graphs. This gives the equation $\sec x =\sqrt{2}.$ 

Recall that $\sec{x} = \dfrac{1}{\cos{x}}.$ Therefore, the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x} & =\sqrt{2} \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡x & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we find the principal value:

$$
x_1 = \arccos \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \right)= 45^\circ
$$

Our first solution lies in the $1$st quadrant and has a reference angle of $\theta_R = 45^\circ.$ Since $\cos x >   0,$ the second solution must lie in the $4$th quadrant, and it also has $\theta_R = 45^\circ.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13979076/assets/c722d4fa2b77011e4df5b086c19bb09943446941484cfaf87559ca39a52183bc.png)

Since the second solution $x_2$  lies in the $4$th quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={360}^{∘}-{\theta }_{R} \\  & ={360}^{∘}-{45}^{∘} \\  & ={315}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solutions for $x\in\left[0^\circ,360^\circ\right)$ are $x=45^\circ, 315^\circ.$ Therefore, the general solution for the given equation is

$$
x = 45^\circ+n\cdot 360^\circ , \quad x=315^\circ+n\cdot 360^\circ ,
$$

where $n$ is any integer.
